the named-note read over an obstructed channel, beside the listing's own arm

summary: `flume friction <name>` reads an absent note off one errno, so a channel present and not a directory reports the note absent on win32 and refuses on posix
acceptance: the read-by-name proves the descent from the root it holds — one call to the shipped composer — so an unreachable channel refuses on every host rather than answering `no note named '<name>'` on one of them
pins: flume friction refuses a named note whose declared channel is present and is not a directory
notes: Verified this tick: `src/cli.ts:795` keys the read's absence on `code !== "ENOENT"`, with no descent from `flumeDir` to the channel it joined at `:774`. The sibling entry moves cli.ts's four other absence arms to `isDirectoryOrAbsentUnder` (`src/fsProbe.ts`) and does not name this one; blocked on it because both edit `src/cli.ts`. No `tests[]`: posix ENOTDIR already refuses through this arm, so the `windows` lane is what the pin protects.
